# PEN-4933 — move the GitHub push credential into a broker sidecar

PR: [#TBD](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/0)

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.ts`
- `src/server/job-manifest.github-publish-broker.test.ts`

## What changed

A new native sidecar, `github-publish-broker`, is rendered into the agent Job
when `adapterConfig.enableGitHubPublishBroker` is set AND the pod inherits at
least one GitHub credential Secret volume. When it is rendered:

- every inherited Secret volume whose mount path matches
  `/etc/paperclip/secrets/github-*token` is mounted into the SIDECAR and is
  removed from the agent container's `volumeMounts`. The volume itself is
  unchanged — same Secret, same `items`, same `optional`, same `defaultMode`;
  only which container mounts it moves;
- the two containers share a `/var/run/paperclip-github-broker` `emptyDir`
  carrying a unix socket, and a `/tmp` `emptyDir` (so the broker can read the
  file-backed bodies `gh` is given);
- the agent container gains `PAPERCLIP_GITHUB_BROKER_SOCKET`;
- the sidecar runs the same image as the agent, as uid **1001**, gid 1000,
  `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, all capabilities dropped, `runAsNonRoot`.

Default is OFF. With the flag unset the rendered Job is byte-identical to
before.

## Why

PEN-3183 decided (§1 D1) that enforcement of the GitHub egress door moves
credential-side. Three of its four bypasses are closed; the survivor — "call
`/usr/bin/git` directly" — is a publish path for exactly one reason, which is
that the push credential was mounted `defaultMode: 292` (0444) into the agent's
own container and `test -r` succeeded from uid 1000. Image-side work cannot
close it: the agent and the egress wrapper are one principal, so any binary the
wrapper may exec the agent may exec directly (§3). The credential is also the
single choke point behind all three doors — `git`, `gh` and the GitHub MCP
server (§4.1) — which otherwise each carry the identical caller-chosen-`PATH`
bypass.

## The boundary is the container, not the mode

The row that commissioned this asked for the Secret to be mounted "mode `0400`
owned by that uid". That is not reachable through a Kubernetes Secret volume: the
kubelet creates the files owned by `root`, so `0400` denies the broker's uid as
readily as the agent's, and the usual way round it — `fsGroup` — is pod-scoped
and would hand the agent container a supplementary group instead.

What makes the credential unreadable by uid 1000 is that the mount is not in the
agent's mount namespace at all. The mode it is mounted with is then doing no
work, and saying otherwise would be the kind of overclaim §8 prohibits. The uid
split is kept because Security asked for it and because it is real defence in
depth against a future `shareProcessNamespace`, but it is not the mechanism.

## Behavioural consequence, and why it is gated

With the flag on, an agent that calls `/usr/bin/git`, `gh` or the MCP server
directly — with any `PATH` it likes — has no credential to authenticate with.
That is the intent. It is also a change to every agent's publish path at once,
and §6 names "breaking every agent's ability to publish" as the reason D4 was
deferred, so it ships default-off for a soak.

⛔ The flag is a ROLLOUT gate, not a kill switch on the egress refusals. §6
records, pre-emptively, that a flag able to disable a refusal is a flag able to
reopen the disclosure path under incident pressure. Turning this one back off
after enablement returns the fleet to the §7 residual and needs Security, not an
incident channel.

## Not addressed here

The uid split means the broker writes into a repository owned by uid 1000 (a
push updates remote-tracking refs). It runs with gid 1000 and `umask 0002`, but
a `.git` subdirectory created earlier by uid 1000 under the default umask is
`drwxr-xr-x`, and a ref write into one of those will fail. This has not been
exercised against a real cluster — it is the specific thing the soak is for, and
it is why the gate exists rather than being a formality.
